transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-11
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Samantha Li (Redwood AE), Marcus Patel (Redwood SE), Diane O'Neill (Redwood CSM), Nina Kapoor (Veridian Head of MLOps), Jordan Reeves (CTO), Leo Park (Infra), Amelia Santos (Procurement)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Veridian requesting capacity increase and EU private deployment. Discussed SLA targets and KMS. Pricing and pilot timeline to be followed up.

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Samantha (Redwood AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining. We have Sam, Marcus, Diane on the Redwood side. Hi Nina, Jordan, Leo, Amelia. Quick agenda — renew, talk uplift in capacity, EU VPC pilot, and then procurement next steps.
[00:00:18] Nina (Veridian): Hey thanks. We're running a bit higher Q4->Q1 than we forecasted so want to lock in a 12 month extension and maybe bump reserved capacity plus add EU region. Wanted to use this call to cover any blockers.
[00:00:34] Jordan (CTO): Yep, need predictable latency for our customer-facing features. We had two incidents where tail latency spiked during batch job window, trying to avoid that.
[00:00:45] Marcus (Redwood SE): Understood. Do you have the current traffic profile handy, like concurrency and p95 token sizes? That helps with batching/kv cache config recs.
[00:00:58] Leo (Infra): We do, I'll share the spreadsheet afterwards — typical concurrency around 600 steady with spikes to about 1.2k for 20-30 minutes. Payloads usually ~350 tokens p95.
[00:01:12] Samantha: Helpful. Two commercial options we discussed earlier — a reserved capacity uplift with a burst buffer, or keep current committed but add burst credits. Each has different unit economics.
[00:01:26] Amelia (Procurement): From procurement perspective we prefer predictable monthly commitments, but we need pricing tied to utilization tiers. Also need the SLA language for latency and uptime.
[00:01:38] Diane (CSM): We can include a latency SLO for p95 under the reserved plan with credits for planned maintenance. The SLA addendum will be in the quote.
[00:01:50] Jordan: What's the risk of degraded quality if we try aggressive quantization to save cost? We tested q8 earlier and saw some hallucination increase.
[00:02:02] Marcus: Good point. Quantization can affect perplexity depending on the model and prompt length. For your chat flows we recommend a mixed profile: q8 for background reranks, q4 or int8 for real-time pathways only if we see no regression on your eval set. We can run a regression check during the pilot.
[00:02:21] Nina: EU region — we need private VPC deployment, customer-managed KMS, audit logs, and data residency guarantee for some datasets. Is that supported in the pilot?
[00:02:34] Samantha: Yes. Redwood Private supports VPC + customer KMS. We'll need to validate connectivity and E2E encryption config. Diane will send the onboarding runbook and checklist.
[00:02:47] Leo: What's the timeline for provisioning an EU VPC? We prefer two-week turn up for pilot.
[00:02:56] Marcus: Typical is 2-3 weeks for a single VPC pilot if we have network details and KMS credentials. For a hardened on-prem variant it takes longer.
[00:03:08] Jordan: Can we pin model versions across regions so inference behavior is identical? We saw tiny diffs earlier.
[00:03:15] Marcus: Yes — model pinning and artifact SHA ensures parity. The runtime may choose different kernels per hardware, but we surface that in the model profile and tracer. We'll include the exact hashes in the rollout policy.
[00:03:30] Amelia: Procurement question: do you offer a short-term credit for pilot costs if we convert to extension?
[00:03:36] Samantha: We can do a pilot credit structure as part of the renewal — typically applied as one-time credit upon signing the 12-month extension. We'll include that in the quote.
[00:03:48] Nina: Two technical asks — 1) can you guarantee no cross-tenant KV cache leakage during multi-tenant bursts, 2) detailed audit log format so our compliance team can ingest.
[00:04:02] Marcus: On the KV cache isolation — yes, we namespace and zero the cache on evictions for Private VPC. For hosted we use strong multi-tenant isolation but we'll document details. Audit logs: we emit event streams with request id, model version, tokens in/out, and RTO timestamps — we'll produce a sample schema.
[00:04:20] Leo: Sounds good. For the benchmarks, could Marcus run a regional perf test with our infra team using our trace-level load? Ideally simulate 1.2k concurrency with peaky bursts and same payload distribution.
[00:04:32] Marcus: Absolutely. If Leo can share a synthetic load runner or traces I'll stand up a test harness. We usually run a 2-hour test to capture tail behaviors.
[00:04:44] Jordan: Great. Pricing — we need to see the uplift per GPU hour and the amortized token cost if we move to reserved. Also want clarity on overage rate.
[00:04:56] Samantha: We'll provide a spreadsheet with committed capacity tiers, burst buffer hourly rates, and overage percentages. I'll add a line for EU region premium and a one-time VPC provisioning fee.
[00:05:09] Amelia: For the contract, who signs the SLA addendum? Do you accept e-sign?
[00:05:14] Diane: We accept DocuSign. We'll route the addendum to your procurement contact. Typical turnaround after signature is 5-7 business days to finalize staging.
[00:05:24] Nina: We also want a rollback policy if performance degrades post-rollout — some canaries and automatic fallback to fallback-model. Is that supported?
[00:05:31] Marcus: Yes — Redwood supports canary rollouts, automatic fallback to a compatible model variant, and traffic shaping. We'll propose a canary plan for your release.
[00:05:42] Leo: One more infra nit — network egress considerations for EU region; if we host inference in eu-west1 do you support private peering to our VPC?
[00:05:51] Samantha: We support cross-connect and private peering options; Marcus will share the network requirements doc.
[00:05:58] Jordan: Any competitors offering this same level of private VPC and KMS tie-in? We've had calls with CloudGiant and ModelServe but those had longer lead times.
[00:06:07] Samantha: We find customers choose Redwood for the production-first runtime and the onboarding cadence.
[00:06:12] Nina: Ok let's recap next steps and owners.
[00:06:16] Samantha: Recap: Sam to send renewed pricing + addendum; Marcus to schedule perf benchmark; Diane to send onboarding runbook; Leo to share traffic profile and traces; Amelia to circulate procurement timeline. Agreed?
[00:06:30] Nina: Agreed. Thanks everyone.
[00:06:33] Jordan: Thanks.
[00:06:35] Amelia: Thanks.

(remarks after 06:35 are logistics and calendar items, omitted for brevity)

End of transcript.
